page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.large is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz with 1.0 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of memory, providing a 4.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 118 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and supports a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1707.39 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1810.0, both placing in the average range. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong at 14.13 GB/sec. However, multi-core and multi-threaded metrics fall into the weak category, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3234.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 3403.17. Memory performance is mixed, showing average read-only bandwidth for large blocks at 56.19 GB/sec but weak write bandwidth at 22.47 GB/sec.

The instance exhibits poor performance in cryptographic and extended instruction tests, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 372.25 and a Passmark CPU score of 1986.08. LLM inference speeds are also limited, with prompt processing for a small 135M model scoring in the bottom 10 percent at 145.92 tokens/sec. Given the dedicated ARMv9 cores, average database operation scores, and integrated 118 GB NVMe SSD, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that benefit from local scratch storage and single-threaded execution, such as lightweight database operations, basic web serving, and general-purpose utility tasks.
